item.title: 'A shift in the air': Can young voters turn Texas blue?
item.description: Texas has long been a Republican stronghold. But could that be starting to change? On the eve of themidterm elections, some younger voters are expressing growing frustration with the political establishment. In Austin, the state capital, our special correspondent Tarek Kai spoke to young voters to hear about their expectations and concerns, and to find out whether they think Texas could turn blue. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.description: Ante la imposibilidad de aprobar un proyecto de presupuesto, el primer ministro belga, Bart de Wever , ha presentado este lunes su dimisión y así se lo ha comunicado al Rey Felipe en una audiencia en el Palacio de Laeken. item.title: US midterm elections 2026: What they are, why they matter and when results will be out
item.description: The US midterm elections are set for November 3, affecting Congress and local offices. Voters will select members of the House and Senate, impacting legislative control. Republican majorities currently hold both chambers, with Democrats needing net gains to gain control. Key issues influencing voter decisions include inflation, immigration, and administration performance. Election results will be determined by state officials and may lead to contested outcomes in closely fought races. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Michigan Democrat stuns party to back Republican candidate in critical Senate race
item.description: A high-profile Democratic defection shook Michigan's Senate race on the eve of US midterm elections as Representative Haley Stevens threw her support behind Republican Mike Rogers rather than backing the Democratic candidate, Abdul Al-Sayed, who beat her in the primary race. The move exposed divisions within the party as control of Congress hangs in the balance. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Bulgaria elects Iliana Iotova as president, pro-Russia candidate defeats pro-Western rival
item.description: Iliana Iotova has triumphed in Bulgaria's presidential runoff, unseating the pro-western contender, Andrey Gyurov. Her campaign prioritized improving livelihoods, fostering peace, and confronting future challenges. This historic win makes Iotova the first female president elected directly by the Bulgarian populace. With security concerns heightened by recent drone attacks in the Black Sea, low voter turnout reflected the deep political rifts concerning Bulgaria's relationship with Russia. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
